incident-bot: :rotating_light: SLO ALERT: dedicated-eu-7 streaming p99 > 3s (SLO watcher). paging @Anna (on-call). snapshot: p95=1.1s p99=4.6s queue_depth=2,120 warmup_fail_rate=46% ingestion_errors=0.5% — runbook: /runbooks/dedicated_warmup.md
Anna (on-call): ack. i'm on call. will triage now. tagging SRE/EngOps/Platform.
Ravi (SRE): grabbing traces. early signal: big short burst at 09:08 UTC, queue amplification to eu-7 pool. autoscaler added nodes but they never transitioned to Ready — warmup timeouts and repeated handshake retries. streaming clients seeing chunk pauses ~8-12s.
Jess (EngOps): if autoscaler is slow, i can force-add two hotshot nodes and prepopulate KV. decision: add 2x hotshot-gpu-small or 1x hotshot-gpu-large? smaller nodes win for parallel warmups.
Ian (Platform): host telemetry shows driver init failures on 3 hosts (kernel-driver mismatch after this week's infra patch). fast-warmup toggle might help but we need to avoid customer-visible correctness regressions.
Maya (Support): Priya from OmniApps reporting long gaps in live transcription streams. Priya, can you confirm timelines?
Priya (Customer): yes — started ~09:06, worst around 09:10. Gaps of ~10s. This caused dropped words in live captions. We're on a live demo. Please escalate.
Anna (on-call): ok plan: 1) Jess manual prewarm + add 3 hotshots 2) Ravi try route fallback to hosted for non-sensitive traffic to relieve pool 3) Ian roll driver restart on suspect hosts + fast-warmup toggle 4) Maya inform customer and track SLA. I'll coordinate.
Jess (EngOps): executing commands now: 
```
# scale + prewarm
redwoodctl pools adjust --pool dedicated-eu-7 --min 6 --target 10
redwoodctl pools prewarm --pool dedicated-eu-7 --mode hotshot --count 3 --kv-preload true
```
Starting prewarm...
Jess (EngOps): prewarm in progress; 2 nodes reached ready at 09:13, one node stuck in driver-init for 45s. marking that host for reprovision.
Ravi (SRE): trace correlation: queue depth peaks line up with the period where desired_nodes>ready_nodes. autoscaler attempts: 
```
09:09:42 autoscaler: target+3
09:10:12 warmup: kv preload timeout
09:10:40 serving: handshake retry x5
09:11:00 pool ready: +2
```
Root cause looks like driver init flapping on a subset of eu hosts.
Ian (Platform): initiating rolling driver restart on the three suspect hosts. also toggling fast-warmup for pool (experimental) — note: may slightly increase per-token latency/cost. toggling now.
incident-bot: action logged: manual scale + prewarm + fast-warmup toggle initiated by Jess and Ian. ticket INC-2026-179332 created.
Ravi (SRE): metric check pre/post actions: before: p95=1.1s p99=4.6s queue=2120. after first two hotshots ready (09:14): p95=640ms p99=2.2s queue=820. after fast-warmup + driver restart (09:18): p95=380ms p99=890ms queue=160. Improvement but still taily.
Jess (EngOps): autoscaler now shows desired=10 available=10, but some hosts show degraded warmup handshake latency earlier; reprovisioned one host 09:15 and it came healthy.
Maya (Support): updating OmniApps: "We're actively mitigating an EU streaming latency issue; engineers have scaled the pool and applied mitigations. We'll update in 10 minutes or sooner."
Priya (Customer): thanks, please advise when resolved — live demo is still ongoing.
Ravi (SRE): i can flip a route-level kv bypass for streaming to avoid repeated coldpath retries. risk: extra model fetches and cost, but should remove handshake retry storms. propose: `routes update --pool dedicated-eu-7 --route streaming --kv_bypass true`
Ian (Platform): note: fallback routing to hosted is possible but will break strict isolation for dedicated contracts. prefer KV bypass first. launching KV bypass now. applied at 09:21 UTC.
Ravi (SRE): after KV bypass: p95=320ms p99=610ms queue=70. traces show streaming chunk arrivals normalized, handshake retries dropped ~98%.
Jess (EngOps): warmup success rate rose from 54% -> 96% after node reprovision + driver restart + fast-warmup. autoscaler long-term adjustments needed.
Maya (Support): customer update: "Mitigations applied (pool scaled, kv bypass for streaming). We see latency returning to normal; please confirm on your side."
Priya (Customer): streams are back to real-time. thanks team.
Anna (on-call): great. immediate mitigations successful. follow-ups: - postmortem owner Ian (driver/kernel regression) - autoscaler warmup heuristics (owner Jess + Ravi) include pre-warm triggers for sudden surge detection - document safe usage of fast-warmup and KV-bypass for customer-sensitive pools (owner: Product). Maya to prepare customer incident summary and SLA impact.
Ravi (SRE): adding internal note: consider adding a pre-scale probe that attempts KV preload during scale decision to avoid amplification from warmup failures. also consider backoff on handshake retries to avoid congestion collapse.
Ian (Platform): I'll collect full host logs and escalate to cloud provider on kernel-driver artifact rolled this week to eu images.
Jess (EngOps): filing autoscaler tuning ticket after postmortem. will prototype incremental-add preference for high-burst customers.
Maya (Support): drafting customer timeline + estimated affected % and SLA burn. will attach logs and notes.
Anna (on-call): handing off to Ravi for long-running follow-ups. i'll remain on-call but stepping out as primary. Ravi, please update INC-2026-179332 with timeline and owners.
Ravi (SRE): accepted. status: mitigations applied, streaming p95/p99 within SLO; monitoring for 2 hours. owners: Ian (infra postmortem), Jess (autoscaler tune), Maya (customer comms).
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-179332 acknowledged by Ravi (SRE). paging cleared for Anna (on-call).
Anna (on-call): thanks team. closing active page. note for postmortem: driver/kernel gating before regional image push. :white_check_mark:
